rationale: Economically sensible, but it is a close re-run of the archive's existing winner (Financing-deficit-weighted capacity growth) that changes two things at once (RANK→IND_RANK and 1-year→3-year cumulative gap) while claiming to isolate a single design choice, so any improvement will be hard to attribute and the incremental information over the published external-financing/asset-growth effect is thin.

target_name: Total outlay expansion with weak working-capital solvency
rationale: The solvency-slack quality leg is a genuinely new dimension relative to the archive's cash-flow and accrual legs, the broadened total-outlay investment measure is well-motivated, and the sign convention matches the hypothesis; the only caveat is mild mechanical overlap since Δinvt appears in both the numerator of the investment leg and inside act.

Both legs are individually familiar (investment intensity, change in asset turnover à la Soliman), but their conditional combination is not a standard published anomaly, the sign is internally consistent, and the deliberate use of different denominators avoids the obvious mechanical artifact.

The accounting-conservatism channel is interesting and untouched by the archive, but heavy capex mechanically depresses dp/ppegt in the investment year (new gross PP&E added with only partial-year depreciation), so the "quality" leg is partly a deterministic function of the investment leg and the product risks being a nonlinear transform of capex rather than a test of asset-life stretching.

Separating the stock (Δcash) from the flow (3-year cash ROA) of internal funding is a substantive rather than cosmetic departure from the capx-minus-oancf gap, the sign logic is coherent, and the densely reported inputs should improve on the archive's thin coverage.

As a diagnostic it correctly answers the horse-race question, but discarding the deficit magnitude makes the construct predict that shrinking, cash-rich firms underperform — a quadrant that directly contradicts the asset-growth anomaly — so a null result would be uninformative about the interaction rather than about the level effect.
